articles.title: Aurzen Zip tri-fold projector review: mirror anything (without DRM)
articles.summary: The tri-fold Zip projector mirrors the screen on your iPhone or Android device and is so portable and easy to use you’ll want to use it everywhere.
articles.body: Tri-folds are having a moment. There’s that impressive Huawei device, my favorite 3-in-1 Apple charger, and now this: the Zip tri-fold projector from a company called Aurzen. It’s the most gadgety gadget I’ve tested in a long time. The Zip’s heft, texture, and hinge stiffness evokes quality at first touch and it’s impressively bright for a compact battery-powered projector that costs $299. Using it is also a joy. It connects quickly to iPhones over AirPlay and to Android devices over Miracast, Smart View, or similar using Wi-Fi Direct — no hotspot required. It then automatically focuses and aligns the image on any available flat surface including walls, t-shirts, and pillows. It works in both landscape and portrait modes and pairs with Bluetooth headsets for private audio or Bluetooth speakers for a shared experience. The built-in rechargeable battery lasts about 80 minutes in my real-world testing, but you can always plug it into a powerbank or wall jack to extend that. Using it sucks, however, if you’re trying to stream from services like Netflix and Disney Plus or trying to watch Spotify music videos. That’s because all those companies protect their content with DRM, and Zip’s mirroring feature “doesn’t meet HDCP content protection standards,” according to a popup message I received when trying to stream video from Amazon Prime. Otherwise, it mirrored everything I could see on my iPhone, Mac, and Android phone, including Plex videos, games, locally stored media, PDFs, PowerPoints, and every app that I opened. The Zip is so easy to carry and set up that I’ve been using it almost daily over the last few weeks. [Product: Aurzen Zip projector | I used it on a 10-hour train ride to watch downloaded movies with Bluetooth headphones. I’ve used it in the bedroom paired to a Bluetooth speaker to watch a film streamed over Plex with my wife after the kids took over the television. But mostly I’ve been using it on any suitably flat surface to aimlessly flip through my social media feeds or play some casual games on a screen that’s much larger than my iPhone. A friend said he’d love to borrow the Zip projector for PowerPoint presentations at client sites, and I can see it playing a recurring role in my vanlife adventures to come. The Zip’s Z-shape works either upright for films and YouTube, or on its side for full-screen portrait video favored by TikTok and Instagram Reels. When upright, you can easily adjust the hinges to get just the right angle and image size. When sideways you have to get more creative to avoid obstacles. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The autofocus works well, but the auto-keystone correction has a very limited range and works best when the Zip is placed directly in front of the projection surface. If you don’t like the results you can give the projector a little shake to try again — just don’t expect miracles. The Zip’s base is metal so it can be affixed to magnetic mounts, including Aurzen’s own $25 suction-mount. If streaming services are critical to your usage, then Aurzen offers a bulky $65 CastPlay HDMI dongle as a work around. Modern phones with USB-C ports that support video output can then stream DRM-protected content directly to the Zip using a USB-C to HDMI adapter. It works on my iPhone 15 Pro and Oppo Find X3 Pro with a random adapter I purchased on Amazon for $7, but adds too much cost and complexity to a device that thrives on its simplicity. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Zip projector is great for anyone traveling light, without a laptop or tablet, that still wants a big(ger)-screen entertainment option for the phone they’re carrying. It’s best in dark rooms, but works surprisingly well during the day so long as you don’t mind viewing a smaller image to concentrate all that LED projected light. Color saturation and contrast aren’t great, but they’re passable, even at the Zip’s 720p resolution. --- Specs * Built-in rechargeable 5000mAh battery * Wi-Fi Direct * Bluetooth 5.4 * 84 x 78 x 26mm (3.3 x 3.1 x 1 inches) * 280g (9.88oz) * On-device power, brightness, volume controls, and capacitive menu buttons * Fan produces about 30dB (from one meter) in brightest mode * Dual 1W speakers * 100 ANSI lumens * 720P resolution * AurzenHub remote control app is available for iOS and Android --- Aurzen tells me that the Zip — currently available for $249 early bird pricing on Kickstarter — will cost $299 starting March 1st. Both prices seem reasonable for the experience provided. The average price will eventually rise to about $349 once it moves to Amazon which is a bit steep for a portable projector that can’t easily stream your favorite shows. Update, March 2nd: Added price increase to $299 and testing of Aurzen’s HDMI dongle to stream DRM-protected content. Photography by Thomas Ricker / The Verge

articles.title: Marvel Will Reveal the Truth About That Deadpool & Wolverine's Crying Thor Flash-Forward, Ryan Reynolds Promises
articles.summary: Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind Deadpool & Wolverine's mysterious flashforward with Thor — eventually, at least.
articles.body:
Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind that mysterious Deadpool & Wolverine flashforward featuring Thor — eventually, at least.

Interviewed by Entertainment Today , Reynolds was asked about the curious moment in his hugely successful Wolverine team-up movie where Deadpool appears to glimpse a future version of himself lying gravely injured, while Chris Hemsworth's Thor looks tearfully on.

"Don't we all want to know why was Thor crying? I want to know too," Reynolds teased. "We will find out at some point. And I'm excited for people to find out."

Deadpool & Wolverine: Our Biggest Burning Questions

Could the moment be coming in Avengers: Doomsday or Avengers: Secret Wars? Here, Reynolds appeared to plead complete ignorance of his potential role in either film, despite having appeared at both San Diego Comic-Con and D23 this summer to help promote the movie.

Asked about his recent humorous appearance with Hugh Jackman where the two stars appeared to beg for a role in Doomsday, Reynolds said he "still didn't know" what that clip meant (this seems extremely unlikely) and that there was "a lot to unpack" in it (there really was not).

Reynolds' involvement in Doomsday was stated last year by The Hollywood Reporter, so there's really no question around whether he will actually turn up. So far, however, Marvel appears to be keeping its focus on promoting Doomsday with the movies (many) major players: the Avengers, New Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men.

Earlier this week, Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo defended shooting the film without a finished script , stating that their improvisational style of production was where "the magic happened."

articles.title: This Week's Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Is the Worst Episode of the Season, But It Still Manages to Give Pike Some of His Best Scenes Ever
articles.summary: Episode 7 of Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, “Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass,” is a frustrating reminder of the potential that the show once held.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 7, “Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass.”

Man, this episode. Five minutes into it, I was ready to tear it apart, but then it had to go and turn into an actual serious story about what is essentially the tragedy of Captain Pike’s life . And not just that, but how he is learning to accept the unfair circumstances of his situation and still be thankful for the moments of beauty and grace and family that he has been afforded in his time, however brief (or cosmically/paradoxically long) that time has been.

Which isn’t to say that I’m not going to tear into this episode some, because it is mostly a waste of what precious little time we have left with Strange New Worlds. Yeah, it’s the “soap opera episode,” and man, at this point I don’t know who the showrunners think they’re aiming some of these stories at.

Rhys Darby is back as Trelane (although they still don’t quite refer to him that way onscreen), the Q-like (or should we just say Q at this point?) being who plagued the crew last season in “Wedding Bell Blues” and who, of course, will also eventually cause problems for the Enterprise when Captain Kirk is running things, as seen in The Original Series episode “The Squire of Gothos” (where he was played by William Campbell). This time around, Trelane has forced the Enterprise crew to live out a soap opera – just like on the old tee-vee, dontcha know! – complete with overlit sets, awkward close-ups, ridiculous plot developments, and over-the-top acting.

So yeah, it’s yet another concept/gimmick episode . This is just what this show is now, I guess, and while it’s cute for a few minutes, the soap opera approach is not sustainable for a full-length episode. Which is probably why the show has to switch back to being, you know, a normal Star Trek episode about 36 minutes in. And that’s what’s so frustrating about “Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass” – not that it’s a dumb soap opera riff, but that it’s actually got a great Captain Pike story hidden inside it, albeit one that’s under-serviced because of the dumb soap opera riff.

I’ve given Anson Mount some grief lately about playing Pike in a way that was diminishing the captain and his status as the leader of an entire starship full of officers and crew. But then he comes along and acts the hell out of this episode, which is ultimately about his ongoing sense of loss and grief – and his inability to deal with either, as has been hinted at earlier in the season – over the loss of his lover Marie Batel (Melanie Scrofano) in last season’s finale.

And it wasn’t just Marie that he lost, but also the life that he lived with her – a complete life, where they had a daughter named Juliet (played by Anna Mirodin) and eventually aged into their golden years, all in a mere moment’s time in regular reality. Mount brings it in full force here, as he finally sits with the ship’s counsellor (played by soap opera legend Deidre Hall, of Days of Our Lives fame) and confronts what he’s been through. His memories of his daughter who never existed, and yet did exist – “I taught her to read” – are so touching not only because of the writing, but also thanks to how Mount handles the scene, and it all just further drives home what a wasted opportunity the prior 36 minutes had been.

“Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass” is further hampered by the inclusion of Trelane, who is nothing but a bystander when all is said and done, literally watching events unfold from a TV control room. He’s surprised when Juliet manifests as an evocation of Pike’s subconscious, and he has no bearing on how Pike deals with that situation. He’s just there , presumably because co-showrunner Akiva Goldsman likes TOS, and that just isn’t enough, particularly when the character plays as nothing more than a lame imitation of the William Campbell original.

Questions and Notes from the Q Continuum:

For everyone annoyed – or just wondering – why Trelane keeps showing up in Captain Pike’s era when his apparent first encounter with the Enterprise doesn’t happen until the Captain Kirk era, let’s just keep in mind that Trelane/Q are capable of flitting around in time, and indeed, exist outside of time. So a first appearance isn’t necessarily a first appearance in this case.

Speaking of which, yes, the “Proctor” played by Diane L. Johnstone is wearing a variation of Q’s “judge” costume from TNG’s “Encounter at Farpoint.” Why? At this point for SNW, I guess the answer to such a question is “why not?”

Once we’ve clicked back into the “real world,” La’an (Christina Chong) and Spock (Ethan Peck) have a nice scene which sure plays like the kind of non-closure closure that a break-up often finishes on. La’an saw in Soap Opera Sybok a glimmer of the more human Spock that she perhaps needed when they were together, but the real Spock is more Vulcan than ever here, unable to process what La’an’s going through when she mentions how hard it’s been since things between them ended. It’s another sad and very well acted scene.

What’s the deal with Sybok? Last we knew, he was still out there, waiting for his chance to actually show up on Strange New Worlds after a brief, viewed-from-behind cameo in Season 1 . Getting an Ethan Peck evil twin version here is very whatever, even if it is imaginary, particularly since the expectation after that Season 1 episode was that we would eventually get to see young Spock and young Sybok onscreen together. And man, is the clock ticking on SNW now.

So the OG Enterprise did have a ship’s counsellor!

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Just Dropped a Major Connection to The Next Generation (Not That It Makes Much Sense)
articles.summary: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds just dropped a major connection to The Next Generation, one that would make the rest of Picard's hair fall out...
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 7, “Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass.”

In the latest episode of Strange New Worlds, the nearly omnipotent being Trelane returns to plague the crew of the USS Enterprise once more. As played by Rhys Darby, the character also showed up last season in the episode “Wedding Bell Blues,” clearly intended to be the Trelane we first met back on The Original Series (when he was played by the late William Campbell). And now, Trelane has been all but confirmed to be a member of the other-dimensional race of beings from Star Trek: The Next Generation known as… the Q Continuum!

But let’s back up a sec. While Trelane’s name is never said onscreen in either SNW episode, showrunners Henry Alonso Meyers and Akiva Goldsman have confirmed the character’s identity in interviews . He first showed up back on TOS when he went face to face with William Shatner’s Captain Kirk in “The Squire of Gothos,” an all-powerful creature who turns out to be nothing but a spoiled little kid whose parents have to give him a cosmic spanking by episode’s end.

The thing is, many fans have often speculated that Trelane and his parents were actually members of the Q Continuum. Of course, the concept of Q wasn’t introduced until The Next Generation’s pilot episode, “Encounter at Farpoint,” which aired some 20 years after “The Squire of Gothos.” It was there that John de Lancie first played the pesky frenemy of Captain Picard, but it did always make a sort of sense that Trelane and Q could be related, since they shared several characteristics – among them, near-omnipotence, a capacity for annoying anyone they’re around, and a flair for dressing up in period costumes.

Which takes us to “Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass,” where we see Trelane essentially completing a school project (of which Captain Pike and his crew are the subjects). A “Proctor” (played by Diane L. Johnstone) shows up throughout the episode to judge Trelane’s performance (she gives him a “solid B-” in the end), and wouldn’t you know it? She’s dressed in a costume that is very similar to the “judge” outfit Q wore in “Encounter at Farpoint.”

Surely this is the final non-admission admission from the show’s writers that Trelane is definitively a Q. What more do we need to just accept this as fact and add it to the Memory Alpha database once and for all? After all, back in “Wedding Bell Blues,” de Lancie provided the voice of Trelane’s non-corporeal father, even if he was not referred to as Q onscreen. (The late writer Peter David also wrote a 1994 Trek novel called Q-Squared that placed Trelane as a member of the Continuum, even if that was never considered canon.)

So this all cute and fun, but would any nerdy discussion of this nature be worth its weight in pocket protectors if we didn’t also poke a hole in the whole thing? Because really… it’s not like that judge costume is a standard-issue Q Continuum wardrobe item. De Lancie’s Q wears the outfit in “Encounter at Farpoint” when he transports Picard and other members of his bridge crew to a recreation of “the post-atomic horror” of the mid-21st century. Basically, in that sequence, Q is dressed up like a judge from that time specific period, so the Proctor wearing a version of the same outfit means that… she decided to dress up as a judge from the mid-21st century when grading Trelane’s project? For some reason?

articles.title: Double Fine Shadow Drops Former Xbox Console Exclusive Keeper on PlayStation 5 Today
articles.body:
Double Fine has wasted no time in bringing its curious adventure game Keeper to PlayStation 5, just weeks after the studio was ditched by Xbox.

Keeper is a colorful and dreamy adventure starring a crumbling lighthouse and a mysterious bird. Despite being critically praised, the project failed to find a wide audience on Xbox Series X/S and PC where it debuted last year, and was Double Fine's penultimate project before Microsoft decided to cut ties with the company.

Its arrival on PlayStation isn't a huge surprise — Double Fine has brought other titles to PS5 as well during its now-concluded era of Xbox ownership — though its swift arrival is still notable. Likewise, the fact that this news was confirmed today in Sony's big State of Play broadcast — it's harder to imagine the news appearing in this way had the studio remained under Xbox's thumb.

"Exploring Keeper’s surreal world is a feast for the senses, with every detail from its propulsive score to its Seussian flora and fauna pulling me deeper into its tale," we wrote in IGN's Keeper review , awarding it a 9/10 score.

Earlier this week, Double Fine launched a new Kickstarter campaign to help secure its immediate future, and promised to make Brütal Legend 2 if it raised an impossible-sounding $100 million .

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

articles.title: Crimson Desert's First Expansion Is Releasing Next Month
articles.summary: Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay.
articles.body:
Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay.

During today's PlayStation State of Play, Pearl Abyss announced Crimson Desert: Chartering the Unknown, a brand new expansion for one of 2026's breakout titles. The new DLC will release on October 15 and add city building mechanics, underwater exploration, a ship that players can captain, and much more. The DLC takes place after the main story and continues the story of the game, so players should probably go back and finish the game if they haven't already to prepare for the new DLC.

As of right now, we're not sure how much this expansion will cost, but it certainly won't be free. Those who pre-order will get a free deep sea diver outfit as a nice bonus. If you were already feeling overwhelmed by all the games coming out in September and October, Pearl Abyss is ensuring you'll have something else to sink dozens of hours into.

Crimson Desert debuted earlier this year and immediately became one of the biggest games of 2026 . Players were fond off the game's deep open-world RPG mechanics, allowing for nuanced and rich combat and exploration. It's a game that you can sink countless hours into without getting bored, so it's great to see Pearl Abyss is keeping players well-fed so soon after release.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

articles.title: Until Dawn 2 Reveals Release Date in New Trailer
articles.summary: Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game.
articles.body:
Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game.

During today's PlayStation State of Play, Firesprite showed off a new look at Until Dawn 2, a game that was formally announced this summer . The trailer teases the franchise's signature branching narrative with deadly choices that can radically change the fate of your characters. However, the biggest takeaway is that the game is coming out very soon, much sooner than some of us could have expected.

Until Dawn 2 will release on January 28, 2027 with pre-orders opening on September 10. Pre-orders will get access to an "Until Dawn classic" outfit, Akishima Island holiday outfit, and collectible Dr. Hill bobble heads to find throughout the game. There will also be a deluxe edition, which adds Y2K-inspired outfits for all characters and a Diaramoa of Death which lets players "relive every grisly demise with vignettes exploring unique angles of each fatal outcome."

PlayStation's 2027 line up is already looking pretty strong, as Until Dawn 2 will release in January and less than a month later, God of War Laufey will make its debut on PS5 . There is also a flurry of speculation and rumors that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet will release in the second half of 2027, which could make it one of PS5's best years to date. We'll just have to wait and see what happens, but next year is going to be an exciting time for gamers.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7: Revelation Release Date and Expansions Revealed
articles.summary: Square Enix has announced a release date for Final Fantasy 7: Revelation, concluding its acclaimed remake trilogy.
articles.body:
Square Enix has announced a release date for Final Fantasy 7: Revelation, concluding its acclaimed remake trilogy.

The third and final chapter in its Final Fantasy 7 remake saga will arrive on April 8, 2027, it was confirmed today. That date arrived during Sony's latest PlayStation State of Play broadcast and just mentioned the title's PS5 arrival — though we know the game will launch simultaneously for all platforms , meaning this is when you should also expect its Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S versions, as well as its PC launch via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Following that, two expansions will also be released over the following 12 months. Story DLC 1: Sephiroth and Story DLC 2: Vincent & the Turks are mentioned as part of a Story Expansion pass that's now visible on Steam . No pricing is available yet for this pass, and no further detail on the story content of these DLCs is mentioned, though this confirms that suggested further chapters are on the way — something fans have expected since the pass previously leaked via the Epic Games Store .

All of the game's cast — Cid, Yuffie, Red XIII, Vincent, Barret, Tifa, Cait Sith, and Cloud — made an appearance, with further battle customization detailed. Sidequests will also now play out different depending who you're controlling and, somewhat weirdly, you can skip through dialogue at double speed, making characters sound a bit like chipmunks.

You'll even be able to leap down from the Highwind into the new region of Wutai, parachuting down to ground level like in Fortnite. Once there — and best of all — you'll be able to wile away hours photographing its cats. Speaking of, Red XIII is now the focus of Revelation's compulsive Queen's Blood card game, if you're into that.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Getting a Pair of Limited Edition PS5 Controllers
articles.summary: Rockstar Games and PlayStation have revealed a pair of GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games and PlayStation have revealed a pair of GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers.

During the PlayStation State of Play, we got some unexpected GTA 6 news. PlayStation and Rockstar Games' marketing deal will give birth to two limited edition GTA 6 controllers. One will come in white, the other in black, but both feature the same core design: the VI logo engraved on the touchpad with palm tree etchings around the controller grips. The Grand Theft Auto logo is also etched into the back of the controllers and are rounded out with a sleek, neon purple trim around the bottom half of the controllers.

Pre-orders will open for the controllers through PlayStation Direct on September 10, but fans won't be able to get their hands on them until the game's release on November 19. The controllers will set fans back a whopping $84.99 and you should probably anticipate them selling out quickly given the rabid demand for the game.

The news comes as GTA 6's marketing begins to really ramp up. Last week, Rockstar debuted the first gameplay for GTA 6 and invited select media (including IGN) to participate in previews for the game. Fans have been suffering for years due to Rockstar's extended gaps of silence, but all of that appears to be coming to an end as GTA 6 has locked in its November release date.

PlayStation has also been boasting that GTA 6 will "play best" on PS5 and the game will have unique, exclusive features on the console. The game will take advantage of the DualSense controller's speakers, haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, and the console's Tempest 3D AudioTech. It's unclear if there will be any kind of console bundle for GTA 6, but it seems slightly unlikely now. The announcement of the controllers would've paired well with a bundle reveal, but no such thing was confirmed by Sony or Rockstar.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance: The Final Preview
articles.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance feels like it’s walking a tightrope between being a loving tribute to Final Fantasies past while also taking the series into a cool new direction and telling its own story. Is it going to pull it off? We’ll have to wait and see, but I was very impressed by the hour I spent playing it. From the gorgeous HD-2D aesthetic to the awesome soundtrack and a battle system that can hold its own, Resonance looks like it’s doing all the right stuff.
articles.body:
This might be the prettiest HD-2D game yet.

Visions are a fun gameplay mechanic that get fan-favorite characters from previous Final Fantasy games involved.

The soundtrack is on point based on what I’ve heard so far.

About two minutes into my demo, Final Fantasy Resonance hit me with a word that I’ve never seen before. That doesn’t happen much in a video game these days. The word? “Puissance.” So, like any good writer, the first thing I did was look it up. It’s Middle-English by way of Anglo-French, first used in the 15th century. It means “strength” or “power.” You see, I’d found my way into a strange, crystalline cave where the Vision of Noctis rested. I already had Noctis in my party, but entering the shrine gave me the opportunity to relive the act of acquiring him. The whole thing played out like a montage: moments from Final Fantasy XV played out all around me, and I answered questions about what I’d do if I was in Noctis’s shoes. The more my answers lined up with Nocti’s actions, the deeper our bond would be. None of it mattered of course; I already had Noctis, and I wouldn’t gain additional puissance for redoing it. But I’m glad I did all the same.

Based on my time with it, Resonance has a lot of cool little moments like that. Let’s get the obvious stuff out of the way. Resonance has the most impressive use of HD-2D I think I’ve ever seen. It’s absolutely gorgeous, and you can see it from the overworld. It’s the way the clouds pass gently overhead, the way the wind seems to rustle the grass beneath your feet. What’s equally stunning is the way your character’s spite moves through all of this. HD-2D is gorgeous, but it can sometimes look like your character is a little out of place in the world. Not so here. Your character looks distinct, but it always seems like they fit.

Once I was done chillin’ with Noctis, it was time for me to head to the Wind Shrine and actually do the demo I’d come here to play. I putzed around in the overworld a bit to get a feel for the combat system, but once I felt good, I mounted my Chocobo and headed for the Wind Shrine. The visuals will get most of the ink in previews like this, but you shouldn’t sleep on Resonance’s music. It’s gorgeous. As I rode around on my Chocobo, and the Chocobo theme played (complete with a few callbacks to Swing de Chocobo), I felt right at home. And the battle theme? An absolute banger that I was banging my head to. I wouldn’t be surprised to see it show up at the Distant Worlds concert series sometime in the near future.

Once inside the Wind Shrine, my demo began in ernest. My party was making quick work of the wolves and other monsters scattered about outside, but inside it was time to get serious. Resonance’s combat system is interesting. I had four characters on the field – Rain, Lasswell, Fina, and Lid. Rain was your fire sword boy protagonist, and I loved him for that; Lasswell is your too-cool-for-school swordsman; Fina is an archer who also serves as the party’s healer; and Lid – who is aiming to be the next Cid, more a title in Resonance than a name – most clearly maps to Thief, despite her giant hammer and stone attacks. It’s a fun group, and I enjoyed the way they gassed each other up – or, in Lasswell’s case, was audibly over that – after fights.

That part is traditional Final Fantasy through and through. What makes Resonance different are the Visions I mentioned earlier. See, Visions aren’t just cool callbacks to Final Fantasies past. They’re partners you can equip to your characters so you can call on their strength in battle. You only equip one to each of your party members at a time, but the crew I was rolling with featured some absolute legends. The Warrior of Light was paired up with my boy Rain. Everyone’s favorite twink Cloud Strife was a natural fit for Lasswell. Lid was hanging out with Final Fantasy IX’s Zidane, and the First Lady of Final Fantasy, Terra herself, was swapping stories with Fina.

Like the main party members, each Vision has their own attacks, spells, and special abilities, so it isn’t much of a surprise to see Cloud pulling off Braver or Terra casting spells. Combat itself reminds me of Final Fantasy X, which is to say it’s actually turn-based, not based on the ATB system, and it feels very good, especially when you can do things like have Lid grant someone else her turn or cast spells that ensure your entire party goes before the enemies do.

The other cool thing Resonance does is add a Stagger gauge. Any attack will reduce it, but tag an enemy with its elemental weakness – almost everything in the Wind Shrine was unsurprisingly of the Wind element, which made them vulnerable to Ice spells and attacks imbued with a bit of chill – and you’ll drop that thing to zero in a hurry. Stagger every enemy and you’ll gain access to extremely powerful Resonance attacks, which call in one of your Visions for a “get the hell off my lawn” attack. These are gloriously animated 3D cutscenes, in contrast to Resonance’s lovely HD-2D, and they look pretty rad. Fights are generally quick and snappy, and it’s fun to watch your characters pull off cool attacks or plan to activate a Resonance.

Between fights, I ran around the shrine, riding elevators, finding goodies, and generally Playing a Final Fantasy Dungeon™. I even ran into one of those weird pots that wanted items. I gave him an ether. Life was good. Chill dude, provided you give him what he asks for.

Finally, it was time for a showdown with the boss of my demo: Aether. He was all high and mighty – apparently, folks from the sky look down on us poor land-dwellers – but I’ve played Xenogears before. He wasn’t scaring me. The fight was the hardest of the demo by far, and I was lucky Lasswell had a weapon that piled on Wind resistance. Aether was no joke, and sometimes he’d summon other monsters to help him out. Luckily, I was pretty familiar with my party’s skills by that point, and I knew the right combination of protective spells, attacks, and abilities to take him down. And when things went sideways, I had Phoenix Downs. So many Phoenix Downs. Thank God my team came to the shrine loaded for air.

Final Fantasy Resonance Preview Screenshots

This was also when I got to see my first summon – Siren, who… I have to be honest, didn’t do much, but she did look cool – and the party’s limit breaks, whether it was Fina’s rain of arrows (between this and her and Terra’s healing magic, she was truly the fight’s MVP) or Lasswell styling on ‘em in a duel under the moonlight, cherry blossoms blowing in the wind. But eventually, Aether went down. And there, my demo ended.

Final Fantasy Resonance feels like it’s walking a tightrope between being a loving tribute to Final Fantasies past while also taking the series into a cool new direction and telling its own story. Is it going to pull it off? We’ll have to wait and see, but I was very impressed by the hour I spent playing it. From the gorgeous HD-2D aesthetic to the awesome soundtrack and a battle system that can hold its own, Resonance looks like it’s doing all the right stuff. The cameos are just a bonus. Just… don’t take Zidane to fight Aether, okay? He’s a windy boy. Doesn’t do much. Bring Noctis and his cool fishing animation instead.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

articles.title: 'Naive' Derbyshire Police police staff who leaked information jailed
articles.summary: Two police call handlers have passed on information to their criminal boyfriends, a court heard.
articles.body:
Two police call handlers who "flaunted" their training by looking up and passing on confidential information to criminals have been jailed.

Jessica Fitzhugh and Ellie-Mae Doherty, both 22, accessed personal details about their criminal boyfriends while working for Derbyshire Constabulary.

Fitzhugh, from Belper, admitted unauthorised access to computer material, and Doherty, from Ripley, pleaded guilty to the more serious offence of misconduct in a public office, after she passed on to her partner some of the information she found.

Doherty was jailed for 11 months and Fitzhugh for four months after a two-day hearing at Leicester Crown Court, which concluded on Thursday.

Following the investigation, the IOPC sent evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) and the charges were authorised on 23 March.

Derbyshire Police said both Doherty and Fitzhugh "have left the organisation" and a misconduct hearing would now take place.

Temporary Deputy Chief Constable Michelle Shooter said: "[They] breached the trust and have faced the consequences of their actions."

In sentencing, Judge Timothy Spencer KC called them "naive", describing them as "girlfriends of two undesirable young men".

He said: "Regrettably and for reasons that now you will find impossible to rationalise, you both flaunted the clear training, the clear direction and the clear guidelines you were given by the Derbyshire Police.

"In your case, Ellie-Mae Doherty, it went further because the information you accessed was clearly passed on in two distinct ways at two distinct times."

Fitzhugh started working for the force in January 2023, when she was 19 years old, as a call handler and then a dispatcher, before referring her friend Doherty for a job, who joined as a call handler in September 2023, the court heard.

Both women went through "intense" vetting and were required to read and sign declarations stating that they had no contacts who were "engaged in criminal activities", the court heard.

Prosecuting, Helen Rodger said each had a sexual relationship with men involved in crime, and should have known that these were "disclosable associations".

The first time Doherty accessed information about an incident and passed it on to Robbie Braddock, with whom she was said to be in a relationship, was in December 2023, roughly two months after she completed her control room training.

Doherty shared details about the incident, a fight in which another male had smashed a window, with Braddock.

Rodger said a second incident involving Doherty on 6 March 2024, saw her access details about a search warrant being executed and pass on details about it to the same man as before.

Doherty viewed the details of the incident several times before also checking who was in custody at Ripley custody suite.

Fitzhugh, who was also said to be in a relationship with a man with a criminal record, looked up incidents in spring 2024, out of what the judge called "idle curiosity".

The two women, who met while both working at McDonald's before starting with the force, sat apart in the dock and were accompanied in court by their families.

Spencer speculated that maybe their "friendship has not survived this case" and said "I have little doubt that it will haunt you for the rest of your days".

He said: "It's impossible to recognise the young women who I read about, with such positive qualities, in the women who committed these offences."

Defending Fitzhugh, Elizabeth Power said she had a "lack of awareness" about the "severity of the breaches that she made".

Lowri Butterworth, for Doherty, told the court that she was "acutely aware" and had been using her time since to "give back" to her community.

Both women were charged in April following an investigation led by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) after conduct referrals.

Emily Barry, from the IOPC, said Doherty admitted supplying information to a man with known links to crime within a few months of her joining the force.

"Call handlers are privy to sensitive information and have access to confidential data on police systems," she added.

"It's incumbent on them not to inappropriately disclose information and to only access material for policing purposes."

Barry said the pair were likely to be barred from working in policing again following respective misconduct hearings.

articles.title: Nothing About NHL 27's Hockey Action Is Worse Than It Was Last Year, but Very Little Has Been Made Better Either As the Series Continues to Stagnate
articles.summary: Nothing is worse than last year, but very little is better either.
articles.body:
As it is with so many annual sports series, incremental change has been the name of the game for EA’s NHL franchise for quite some time now. Rather than attempting to drastically alter its foundations, developer EA Vancouver has largely focused on making small tweaks that aim to dial up the authenticity wherever possible. It’s a strategy that continues with NHL 27, an annual entry that mostly feels the same as it has in recent years. The actual hockey remains strong, and there are a handful of small but welcome changes to be found, but the familiar feeling of nearly everything else has otherwise worn thin.

There are no new modes to speak of this year. Staples like Franchise, Build a Pro, World of Chel, and HUT serve as the main options, alongside smaller modes like Ones and Threes, plus tournaments like the World Juniors. The familiarity from past entries even extends to the menus, which look exactly the same as they did in NHL 26. Everything looks so similar, in fact, that some people might think they booted up last year’s game by mistake. There’s an argument to be made for not fixing what isn’t broken, but when a sequel doesn’t look any different right from the start up screens, it feels like a bad sign – especially for a series that often gets critiqued for its lack of differentiation.

In 2024, EA Sports made the decision to move the NHL series exclusively to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. In theory, moving away from the previous console generation should have resulted in prettier graphics, but NHL 27 continues to look stuck in the past. NHL 26 featured some weird areas where team logos would get cut off on specific screens, and while that problem has been resolved or at least lessened this year, there are a lot of other lingering graphical issues throughout.

For one thing, character models are still ugly, and that extends to both hockey personnel and fans in the stands. The crowds are filled with people that look and move like they did multiple console generations ago, and the heroes of the NHL only fare slightly better. Some players look better than others, but hockey helmets help disguise the rougher designs. The same can’t be said for veteran coaches that have spent decades in the league, who sometimes look like poorly recreated custom characters.

What’s frustrating about all this is that there are moments where NHL 27 does visually impress. The surface of the ice continues to look bright and inviting, even as it deteriorates and gets snowed up throughout the course of a game. There are also some nice little details that pop up in unexpected places – at one point while my player was sitting in the penalty box, I noticed several scratches along the surface of the glass, meant to resemble scrapes left by errant shots. For those that have spent a significant amount of time playing the real sport, these accents help things feel more realistic.

For NHL 27, EA Vancouver has also polished up the arenas, putting more effort into making them look closer to their real-world counterparts. If you’ve ever stepped foot in some of these locations, you can feel the authenticity. I’ve been to arenas like Key Bank Center, Benchmark International Arena, and Nationwide Arena, and their digital versions look and feel closer to the real thing than they have in the past. That’s thanks in part to the additional landmarks in each arena, as well as the accurate goal celebrations and Jumbotron videos. These details make NHL 27 feel like a proper celebration of the culture surrounding hockey.

To that end, there have also been big changes to the music selection. I enjoyed a lot of the tracks in NHL 26, but rather than highlighting newer artists that kind of fit with hockey’s themes, this year EA licensed popular tracks you’d be likely to hear when attending or watching games. That means the music selection can be a little older at times, but it feels way more appropriate. I’ve associated songs like Bush’s “Machinehead” and Blur’s “Song 2” with hockey since I was a kid, and these are songs that still get regular play during games. You’ll even hear hype songs that are specific to certain NHL teams, like a track the Dallas Stars commissioned for their 1999 Stanley Cup run (which was the year Brett Hull’s foot was definitely in the crease). There is even a little background on these song selections, as the menus no longer offer just the name of the song and artist, but also a team logo and a small blurb about its history with that club, or with hockey in general. These small lessons quickly proved to be one of my favorite new features.

In the decades since the NHL series began, EA Vancouver has refined its take on hockey to a point where it consistently feels fun and exciting, even if it is all familiar. The gameplay in NHL 27 is more of the same, but that core experience largely remains enjoyable as well. This formula doesn’t need to be rebuilt from the ground up, because it really does work. There’s depth and healthy learning curve, but also plenty of options to tailor the experience to match your skill level or even how much time you have to play. It gets the important elements of hockey right, from the speed and power of the players, to the immense satisfaction of scoring a big goal.

While that was all true last year as well, the addition of playbooks is one of the biggest changes in terms of the on-ice action. The 32 real-life teams of the NHL have a lot of nuances that make them feel distinct from one another, and EA Vancouver has created specific playbooks to reflect that. When selecting a team, there’s now an option to use their assigned playbook, or to switch to one that better matches your own style. For example, if you find that the AI teammates on the Red Wings play too conservatively in the neutral zone, you can choose a playbook that encourages more aggression. Figuring out how these combinations work adds a bit more depth to the package, as well as increased strategy and opportunities for creativity.

Those that enjoy customization options like this have Be a Pro mode to lean on as well, which allows the creation of an original character that can be taken through an NHL career. I’ve often enjoyed this mode because it feels a lot closer to playing the actual sport of hockey; you’re not constantly switching between players on the ice, instead focusing on a single guy. Unfortunately, this is one of the modes most blatantly similar to NHL 26. Press conferences are pretty much unchanged, with the same groan-inducing questions meant to increase (or decrease) your brand and popularity with your fans, teammates, and the organization. Parts of this mode felt stale last year, and basically nothing has been done to breathe new life into it.

The commentary is one area where NHL 27 definitely feels stuck in the past, too. It’s never been particularly great, exacerbated by the fact that nothing feels tailored for the specific teams on the ice. The commentators often refer to checks as a “crunch,” and during one game against the AHL’s Syracuse Crunch, that exact phrase was used. It seemed like the perfect opportunity for some wordplay like “a perfect crunch from the Syracuse Crunch” – it wouldn’t be all that clever, but it would have at least made things sound distinct from all the other times I heard it. No such luck. And then there’s the fact that the exact same comments are made game after game. You can only hear about a “really exciting tilt” so many times before you contemplate shutting this banter off altogether.

It’s not just the audio commentary that’s kind of broken, either. Be a Pro mode shows news headlines between games based on your performance, and they regurgitate the same critiques ceaselessly. If your team wins a blow out but your custom character didn’t score, it’s a “rough night,” with an image of your player looking downtrodden. Even if that’s not a great night for the individual player, it doesn’t quite match what happened on the ice. Additionally, there seems to be even less variety in these headlines than there was in NHL 26.

There are lots of small elements that hurt the immersion in NHL 27. During one game in Be a Pro, I was being pressured to head to the bench late in the third period, but didn’t have a good opportunity to change up. A whistle stopped play with 1.5 seconds left in regulation, and I assumed I’d still be on the ice for this small leftover amount of time. Instead, I found my custom player sitting down for the next face off, which would never happen in a real hockey game. EA Vancouver may have put a lot of effort into making the arenas match their real-life counterparts, but the games that play out within them don’t always match that level of care. For example, home crowds will eventually turn on their team during a blowout, but it’s not immediate – that means you’ll sometimes see fans dancing and enjoying hype songs during an early 3-0 deficit like nothing is going wrong.

articles.title: D&D Long Rest Tavern Has a Clever Premise but I Wish It (Literally) Went Deeper | IGN Preview
articles.summary: Dungeons and Dragons: Long Rest Tavern ended up feeling like a pretty natural fit between world and mechanics in our first hands-on with it. As a management game, it's a little bit on the basic side, but there is added depth to discover as your intrepid customers strike out to win fame and fortune, and maybe cut you in a little bit on the side.
articles.body:
The early game is a bit too hands-off since you have to hire employees to do most of what needs doing.

I really, really wished I could’ve built out on floors above and below rather than just across.

Once it picks up steam, Long Rest Tavern’s gameplay loop gets really enjoyable.

I'll be honest: if any of the D&D parties I've been involved in walked into my place of business, I'd call the militia immediately. That just isn't going to end well. But in the upcoming Dungeons & Dragons: Long Rest Tavern, I was able to serve drinks and offer a warm bed to some of the Forgotten Realms' more well-behaved adventuring bands. It ended up feeling like a pretty natural fit between world and mechanics. As a management game, it's a little bit on the basic side, but there is added depth to discover as your intrepid customers strike out to win fame and fortune, and maybe cut you in a little bit on the side.

Your innkeeper can come from any of the main D&D 5th Edition races and classes, though so far this is purely visual. Druids aren't better at growing hops, as far as I could tell. Regardless of their background, they have found themselves in possession of a run-down, abandoned, haunted tavern by the side of the road. I'd love to have seen the ad, because it definitely seems like kind of a scam at first. But in spite of everything, I took to befriending the resident spirit, cleaning up most of the mess, and getting everything looking nice and cozy.

This rendition of the Realms is very stylized, with a chill and charming storybook aesthetic. The various dwarves, elves, and tieflings that come through the door have big heads and tiny bodies, and are animated with exaggerated emotiveness. This, along with good use of color and contrast, makes it very easy to tell what's going on at any given time from a wyvern's-eye view. Your guests also need to be able to see their meals, though. So in addition to a bar and tables, you'll need to place light sources either on those tables or close by.

It takes at least three to run a tavern, so before I could open for business, I had to hire a bartender and a waiter. These are the tasks that your innkeeper avatar can't do themselves. Each available staff member has different stats to reflect how efficient they are at pouring pints, cooking, waiting tables, and cleaning up. They also come with one positive or negative trait, like taking longer to get tired or levelling up slower. Their daily wages, of course, tend to reflect their skill level. What a wondrous, fantastical world this is!

There is no bar seating in the Long Rest Tavern. Rather, parties will place their orders with the waiter, who then travels to the bar, waits for the bartender to fill the mugs, and then brings them to the table. At least it saves the heroes the trouble of crowding around the taps and trying to wave and yell out over loud conversations to get a refill. It did feel a little odd to me that I couldn't directly help out with this process, since it means a lot of standing around early on. You can talk to an employee to make them work faster for a limited period of time, and it's up to you whether you want to imagine that as a berating or a pep talk. But especially those first few nights it kind of felt like my main job was to stare creepily at my customers.

Once a party has finished their brews and left a proper mess in the process, it was my job to clean up the table to be ready for the next customers. You can eventually hire someone to do this as well, but I didn't have anything better to do, and I was feeling a bit awkward about not contributing anything to the business other than start-up capital I probably inherited from a rich uncle or something. Satisfied guests will leave nice tips and increase the Renown of your tavern as they spread the word, which eventually attracts more prestigious guests.

New opportunities come with new challenges, though. The low-level scrubs who make up your starting clientele are more than delighted to gulp cheap ale by the pint. Kids these days with a +1 Base Attack Bonus and no magic items are always going out to get absolutely trashed on Fantasy Michelob Ultra. But if some proper toughs with a few successful quests under their belt wander in, they're going to start asking for fancy IPAs or whatever possibly cursed liquor the bards in Waterdeep are promoting these days.

And so my little inn took on a side business as a brewery. The ingredients for the lower-level libations can simply be ordered from the local grocer. But more advanced recipes require a bit of danger. We'll come back to that, though, because the next step was getting some beds set up so weary and/or completely sloshed aspiring champions could sleep off their hangovers.

While I appreciated the gradually increasing complexity of running my business, this is where I started to get a bit frustrated with the fact that Long Rest Tavern only features one buildable level. I don't know what the zoning codes on the Sword Coast look like, but it would be really nice to have my brewery down in the cellar and the guest rooms upstairs. Having to fit everything onto a single, somewhat cramped flat surface was a little bit annoying, and made my inn feel less like a real place. If I could make one request, it would definitely be allowing multiple floors.

As my inn became more cramped, though, the world also opened up with the introduction of a regional map that allowed me to share quests with any party who had stayed the night previously. Each quest has a difficulty class that must be beaten by rolling a d20, featuring a great little animation to sell that D&D feeling. And different parties are better suited to some than others, both based on the type of party they are, the type of challenge, their level, and the special traits each of their members might possess.

In exchange for your intel, a successful group of heroes will bring back reagents and ingredients for you that become necessary for higher-level recipes. These concoctions can then attract higher-level parties who can go on more dangerous adventures for more potent and sought-after goodies, and so on. I liked the way this emphasized the role of the tavern in the overall regional adventurer economy. At this point, it really did feel like this was the place newly-created player characters showed up to seek rumors of treasure and glory.

From here, things settled into a comfortable rhythm. By day, my boarders would follow my tips out into the treacherous wilds, hopefully not die, and return with ingredients. By night, I'd serve my latest concoctions to increasingly prestigious and demanding guests – it's even possible, we were told, to get some big shots like Minsc from the Baldur's Gate series passing through. And as my treasure chest swelled, I unlocked new machines like a cider press and fresh decorations to keep the new guests impressed. Adding more bedrooms means being able to get more quests done.

This is all accompanied by some delightfully jaunty tavern music, though it comes from nowhere in particular. It would have been neat if I could invite different bards to play and entertain my guests and staff. There are a couple other odd limitations, too, like the fact that the starting bar counter – the only one I saw, though it's possible something bigger unlocks later – can only stock two kinds of drinks. So it didn't take long for me to have far more recipes than I was allowed to serve, which felt unfortunate.

The next step is adding food to the menu, and I only got to mess with that a little bit in the time I had with the demo. All in all, despite its limitations, running a small business in a recognizable fantasy setting was both rewarding and relaxing in Dungeons & Dragons: Long Rest Tavern. Getting to roll some dice during the day is a snappy, exciting shot of adventure to break up the evenings of running around cleaning up after the intrepid heroes of the Realms. And the steady stream of unlocks kept me wanting to grow my little establishment, even as it made me lament the lack of stairs.

You'll be able to pull up a chair at the tavern yourself in 2027.

articles.title: Crunchyroll Game Vault Officially Crosses Over 100 Games With 3 New Additions
articles.summary: The addition of three new anime-inspired game has brought Crunchyroll's Game Vault into the triple digits.
articles.body:
Crunchyroll’s Game Vault has officially crossed over 100 games.

The Game Vault originally launched back in 2023 with a limited number of titles, largely connected to various anime series and properties. The recent addition of three new games has brought the vault's total to 101, and now Crunchyroll is offering a look at what’s next for the anime-themed gaming service.

The Game Vault is exclusive to Mega and Ultimate Fan subscribers , who also get access to the service’s anime streaming library, the Crunchyroll Store, and the recently launched Crunchyroll Manga service. You can check out the full Game Vault library here .

The Crunchyroll Game Vault recently launched three new games that brought its full catalog into the triple digits. All of these games are playable on mobile with touch screen controls or through a browser, where you can use a mouse and keyboard or connect your own PC-compatible controller.

Crunchyroll Game Vault will also soon be publishing its first original game. Developed alongside TMS Entertainment and independent developer The MIX, pre-registration is now open for the cat-collecting game Bananya Buddies .

Here's a look at more games coming to the service in the near future:

ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs (tinyBuild)

Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon (Yacht Club Games)

Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley (Raw Fury)

These new additions join an existing lineup of anime-related games like Steins;Gate, Corpse Party, and Metal Slug Tactics.

Crunchyroll has been going through quite a few shifts since it was brought under the Sony umbrella back in 2021 . It removed its free ad-supported tier at the end of 2025 before hiking prices in early 2026 . Since then, the service has been focused on making its plans worth the more expensive cost.

The Crunchyroll Store is now restricted to Mega and Ultimate fan subscribers, and is moving toward exclusive and limited-time merch drops, starting with a Chainsaw Man collab . The Crunchyroll Game Vault is yet another benefit for these specific subscription tiers. It’s a unique library in the grand scheme of gaming subscriptions , but it’s worth checking out for anyone who already subscribes to Crunchyroll for the anime streaming .

articles.title: Nvidia’s new RTX Spark laptops launch in October with two different configs
articles.summary: Nvidia’s N1X laptop will ship in two different configurations for laptops and mini PCs.
articles.body: All the rumors leading up to Nvidia’s announcement of its Arm-based RTX Spark chips over the summer mentioned two specific chips: the N1X and N1. While the N1 won’t be arriving this year, Nvidia says its N1X chip is arriving in RTX Spark laptops in two different configurations in October. You’ll be able to buy an RTX Spark N1X laptop with a configuration that I would call the mini PC chip. The top of the line N1X chip comes with a 6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU, paired with a 20-core Grace CPU and between 24GB and 128GB of unified memory. This particular chip will ship in both high-end laptops and miniature PCs like Microsoft’s Surface RTX Spark Dev Box. [Image: N1X configurations available in October. The more cut down N1X, or what I’d call the laptop chip, has a 5120-core Blackwell RTX GPU, combined with an 18-core Grace CPU and between 24GB and 32GB of unified memory. I’d expect most RTX Spark N1x laptops are going to use this chip, with devices launching from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, or MSI in October. We’re still waiting for Nvidia to share more on what the N1X is capable of for laptop gaming, but the company is vaguely promising 100fps 1440p gaming with ray-tracing and DLSS enabled for now. RTX Spark laptops are only a month away, so we’re also waiting to hear about exact availability and pricing from PC makers. With a RAMageddon crisis still looming large, I’m expecting to see N1X laptops priced at the very premium end of the market.

articles.title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Leads String of No-Shows During Sony's September 2026 PlayStation State of Play
articles.summary: Sony's State of Play for September 2026 has now concluded without any sign of Naughty Dog's upcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, as well as many other first-party PlayStation games that fans had hoped to see.
articles.body:
Sony's State of Play for September 2026 has now concluded without any sign of Naughty Dog's upcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , as well as many other first-party PlayStation games that fans had hoped to see.

The showcase was notable for its string of other no-shows, including further updates on God of War: Laufey, Horizon Hunters Gathering, Fairgames, and any kind of update for what will happen to Bungie's Marathon.

The wait also continues for more news on what several other PlayStation Studios are working on, including Dreams maker Media Molecule and Days Gone studio Sony Bend. It has now been six years since Media Molecule last shipped a game, and seven since Bend first launched Days Gone.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

Ahead of the showcase, hopes were high that Naughty Dog would bring the curtain down on today's proceedings, particularly as the studio broke its relative radio silence this week to confirm that it had now completed Intergalactic's performance capture . In hindsight, this confirmation now feels more like an acknowledgement that no other update would be provided today, with word that the project was progresing simply provided instead. Naughty Dog last shipped an all-new game in 2020, with The Last of Us 2, though has spent time since on various remakes, and its now-scrapped multiplayer The Last of Us spinoff.

With less than six months to go until release, God of War Laufey seemed likely to appear today, though Sony did spend considerable time on the game back in July. As for Sony's multiplayer Horizon spinoff, its own no-show seems to align with the recent Bloomberg report that Sony was unhappy with feedback to the game's public playtest, with the game now from being a live-service title to one based around co-operative play with a story mode.

What on earth is going on with Fairgame ? It's a fair question. Built by Haven Studios, the developer previously set up by Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond, this live-service heist game has not been glimpsed for years. Last year, it emerged Raymond had departed the company . A few months later, Fairgame's creative director followed suit . Raymond's last shipped game remains Star Wars: Battlefront 2, which EA published back in 2017.

And finally, there's Marathon , being worked on by the remains of Bungie. With Destiny 2 development dead after a decade and hundreds of staff laid off , there's been little word on what the future holds for Bungie. But as Marathon's player numbers dwindle, the question must be asked how much longer it too will be considered worth supporting. And all of this amid constant calls even now for a Destiny 3 .

At the end of the day, though, does any of this matter? In just two months' time, Sony will watch as Grand Theft Auto 6, the biggest game of this console generation, is released alongside marketing telling prospective GTA customers that the game plays best on PS5 . Today was not a great showcase of Sony's first-party output, but with GTA 6 fast approaching, it's fair to suggest that there may be better moments to make big announcements.

For everything that did make it into today's showcase, catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

articles.title: 'We Were All Positive It Was Going to Fail': Rockstar Devs Thought GTA Online Would Flop
articles.summary: A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched.
articles.body:
A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched.

In an interview with Eldorado , ex-Rockstar Games developer Matt Freedman looked back on the success of GTA 5 and attributed a lot of it to GTA Online. He noted that a lot of investors seek a GTA Online-level success nowadays, but said it was treated as an "afterthought" during its initial development.

"When we were working on GTA Online, it was an afterthought," said Freedman. "We were all positive it was going to fail. Everyone thought this thing was going to fail. I remember QA testers coming up to me [and saying], 'We’ve got four hours of content for online mode. To do everything in GTA Online, it’s four hours,' or it was something like that. It was really short, and they’re like: ‘We are in so much trouble,' and we’re all sitting there going, 'Let’s see what happens. We’re going to do our best job anyways.' And then it took off, and then there was, to Rockstar’s credit, a fast follow with as much content as possible and [it] just kind of keep it going. And now it’s become this phenomenon."

It's unclear when the perception of GTA Online's potential began to shift at Rockstar. The studio did seem to have ambitions for it before launch, as it released a sizable trailer and media previews for the online mode before the game's release with plans for post-launch content like heists. Still, Freedman is right that the game was pretty light on content upon arrival. There wasn't a ton to do beyond the typical sandbox mayhem and the most exciting content in the game didn't arrive until years later, including its heists update.

Still, Rockstar worked hard to support it, even if its success did seem to catch the company off-guard. Rockstar Games had plans for GTA 5 single player DLC, which was scrapped after GTA Online took off and required more resources. It also reportedly wasn't feasible to do both while also developing Red Dead Redemption 2, so Rockstar leaned into GTA Online.

It's also hard to imagine that the studio anticipated GTA Online running for as long as it has. 13 years later, GTA Online is still getting massive updates and despite GTA 6's release on the horizon, the team may well keep supporting it while it keeps being profitable. GTA 6 will be a "single player experience" when it launches and Rockstar has been cagey about its plans for online beyond that. It also just announced its official nopixel RP server for the PC version of GTA 5 , which shows a pretty high level of commitment.

articles.title: Microsoft Announces Big Changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming, Switches to Monthly Hour Limits
articles.summary: Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits.
articles.body:
Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits.

From November, Game Pass plans will include a set number of cloud gaming hours each month:

Xbox Game Pass cloud gaming monthly limits:

Once subscribers use their included hours, they can buy additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Currently, Game Pass subscribers can stream without these monthly hour limits. The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers.

Also in November, Microsoft said players will be able to buy cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and ‘stream eligible games they own on supported devices’ without subscribing to Game Pass.

In a blog post , Microsoft said it was making the changes because the cost of providing cloud gaming has grown as more people use it and play for longer. The monthly limits, Microsoft continued, will mean it can invest in reliability and performance. But it said it understood that for some players the practical result is a higher cost.

Expect more information on pricing, purchasing additional hours, eligible games, market availability, and how players can check their remaining time in November. Microsoft also said it’ll keep a close eye on feedback and may tweak the offering before the changes come in.

Cloud gaming has become an increasingly important part of the video game offering as the RAMpocalypse makes console gaming increasingly expensive. Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently predicted the video game industry will be in “commercial streaming mode” within three years — but for video game streaming to matter, it would have to run GTA 6 just as well as consoles do.

During an investor focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, Zelnick was asked for his thoughts on the video game industry as it buckles under the pressure of skyrocketing chip costs, which have forced Sony and Microsoft to raise the price of their consoles and potentially delay the launches of the PlayStation 6 and the next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix.

Zelnick admitted the rising cost of hardware “is not a good thing,” because cheaper hardware means more hardware in people’s hands, which is what software companies desire. But he suggested the advent of video game streaming would go a long way to tackling this problem.

Both Sony and Microsoft are predicted to lean heavily on streaming in the coming years as they contend with the RAMpocalypse. “I just don't have any insight as to what the console manufacturers have planned, but it wouldn't at all surprise me if part of what they plan is streaming,” Zelnick offered.

In the shorter term, GTA 6 launches in November and it is expected to boost console sales significantly. And there are a number of use cases with cloud gaming that could make it a popular option for those either without a current gen console, or who are priced out of buying one. For example, Xbox Cloud Gaming is used by some Xbox One owners to play current gen games. It’s also used by some PC gamers to play games that are beyond their current machines. Some people use cloud gaming to sample Game Pass games before installing — although this of course won’t apply to GTA 6. Others use cloud gaming to extend playtime in rooms in which they don’t have a console — perhaps they’re at work or away over a weekend. So, while Microsoft may say GTA 6 has nothing to do with the November changes to Xbox cloud gaming, it’s hard to see past the timing here.

As for the price of cloud gaming time, don’t expect a ‘pay as you go’ system — Microsoft will sell batches of hours, and those hours won’t expire. That means there’s no pressure to use your hours before they disappear.

In July, Microsoft launched a test for ad-supported Xbox game streaming , promising the ads wouldn’t interrupt gameplay. “For many players, the device they already own now allows them to stream games with Xbox,” Microsoft said at the time. “Cloud can also help Xbox One owners play newer games built for Xbox Series X|S without needing to purchase new hardware right away. That can be especially meaningful in places where consoles are harder to find or less affordable, giving more players another way to access great games on devices they already have.”

The test of ad-supported Xbox streaming arrived amid console price rises that are pushing some gaming hardware towards the $1,000 mark. In June, Microsoft announced significant price rises for Xbox consoles , blaming the ongoing “components crisis.”

“Last October, we increased Xbox console price by 20-70 in the U.S.,” Microsoft said at the time. “We hoped another price increase would not be necessary, and we have spent the last several months working with suppliers on options. Unfortunately, console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027.

"The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles. Unlike phones, computers, speakers, and other consumer devices, consoles are typically not sold at a profit, but instead for less than they cost to make.”

New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March , blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped , instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

articles.title: Microsoft opens up Xbox Cloud Gaming with new pay-as-you-go option
articles.summary: Microsoft is trying once again to tempt people without an Xbox into its ecosystem.
articles.body: Microsoft says it will let anyone access Xbox Cloud Gaming in November, without the need to subscribe to Xbox Game Pass. The change to a pay-as-you-go model is part of some sweeping changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming today, and is designed for people who don’t use cloud access enough to warrant a monthly subscription. “Players will be able to purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices,” says the Xbox team. “This will provide another option for people who want occasional access to cloud gaming or do not want a recurring Game Pass subscription.” This pay-as-you-go model comes alongside some major limits on cloud gaming for Game Pass subscribers. Microsoft is imposing monthly hour limits, with Ultimate subscribers limited to just 15 hours each month. This could force many Game Pass subscribers to pay for hourly bundles, or use cloud gaming less. The pay-as-you-go option seems to be targeted more at gamers who don’t own an Xbox, or those who primarily play from a phone. Microsoft is also testing free, ad-supported cloud gaming for Xbox Insiders, which could also help open cloud gaming access to more people without an Xbox. Microsoft has been trying to attract more players to its Xbox ecosystem through cloud and mobile for years now. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has even set an ambitious and nearly impossible goal to make Xbox “one of the few companies that entertains more than a billion people each day.” Microsoft previously tried to launch an Xbox mobile store, with the aim of allowing people to purchase an Xbox game and then immediately stream it to their device. The company started rolling out the ability to purchase games and DLC inside its Xbox mobile app last year, but it had to remove the remote play option to adhere to Apple’s App Store policies. You still can’t buy an Xbox game in the Xbox mobile app on iOS and then stream it inside that same app. Apple’s policies force people to manually navigate to the Xbox Cloud Gaming mobile website on a browser to get access to cloud gaming. Microsoft blamed the delay to its Xbox mobile store on Apple last year, and also said in 2024 that it had built an Xbox game store for Android that it couldn’t launch due to Google’s store policies. Microsoft has continued to battle legally to try and open up Apple and Google’s stores, and Xbox chief Asha Sharma said earlier this year that the “idea” of an Xbox mobile store “is not dead.”

articles.title: Microsoft slashes Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 hours a month for Ultimate subscribers
articles.summary: The new cloud gaming hourly restrictions come nearly a year after all Game Pass subscribers got cloud access.
articles.body: Microsoft is announcing some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming today, less than a year after opening up cloud gaming to its Xbox Game Pass Premium and Essential tiers. While all Game Pass plans have included unlimited cloud gaming over the past year, from November this will be limited to just 15 hours on Ultimate, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and a measly 5 hours for Game Pass Essential. “We recognize that introducing limits is a meaningful change, particularly for players who regularly spend more time gaming through the cloud,” says the Xbox team in a blog post announcing the changes. “We expect this upcoming change to impact four percent of Game Pass subscribers.” If you want to use more than the 15 hours included with Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, you’ll need to purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox store starting in November. Microsoft isn’t revealing exact pricing and details today, but Xbox cloud players will be able to purchase bundles of hours that can roll over if unused in a particular month. Microsoft says it’s making these changes “because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer.“ While that’s undeniably true, Microsoft previously restricted Xbox Cloud Gaming access to its Game Pass Ultimate tier and then opened up access to all tiers of Game Pass nearly a year ago. Unlimited cloud gaming was one of the big additions for Game Pass Premium and Essential tiers, and now that everyone has gotten used to the new feature, they’re being asked to pay for more hours. Xbox players use cloud gaming in a variety of different ways, including people trying out games before they download them, Xbox One owners using it to access Xbox Series X games, or gamers simply accessing Xbox games away from home on mobile devices. These strict monthly limits could force some Xbox One owners to upgrade their consoles instead of relying on the cloud for certain games. Players who have regularly used Xbox Cloud Gaming to try out games might also think twice about doing that regularly, especially when the hourly restrictions could make that a lot more difficult on the Game Pass Essential tier. As part of these sweeping changes, Microsoft is also opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming access to people without a Game Pass subscription. “Players will be able to purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices,” says the Xbox team. “This will provide another option for people who want occasional access to cloud gaming or do not want a recurring Game Pass subscription.” I don’t think these limits are going to go down well with Xbox Game Pass subscribers, much like the original price hikes. Microsoft was forced to drop the price of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate six months later, but cut new Call of Duty titles from the service in a bid to balance its costs. These latest Xbox Cloud Gaming changes seem like yet another attempt to prevent more Game Pass price increases.

articles.title: The Odyssey Is Extending Its IMAX 70MM Run Once Again Through the End of September
articles.summary: If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026.
articles.body:
If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026.

The Odyssey's historic IMAX run was supposed to end on September 15, but the "overwhelming public demand" behind this decision will now see the film staying in the format it's "intended" to be seen for 11 weeks.

If you want to see it for yourself, check out the showtimes right here.

Since it first premiered on July 17, The Odyssey has become the highest-grossing IMAX release of all time, earning $457 million at the global box office. The IMAX 70MM screenings alone have accounted for $66 million of that across the 41 theaters that feature it. These accolades are fitting, as The Odyssey was also the first film to ever be shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

Per Box Office Mojo, The Odyssey has surpassed $1.55 billion at the global box office and will look to extend that run over the course of September as it races toward $2 billion.

In our The Odyssey review, we said that it "adapts Homer through a new eye that brings a sense of horror and existential angst to the story – and some humor too. It may not be a perfect movie, but it’s a pretty great moviegoing experience all the same."

articles.title: New Dave Bautista Video Reveals He's Putting On a Ton of Muscle to Play Kratos in God of War
articles.summary: Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV series.
articles.body:
Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV show.

Bautista was officially cast as Kratos in the God of War TV series last month and he has wasted no time prepping for the role. The actor shared a video on Instagram flexing his new physique, noting that he has been weight training for three weeks and has two months to "get to where he needs to be."

Unlike other roles where an actor might have six to twelve months or more to prepare, Bautista has to hit the ground running. The God of War TV series began shooting earlier this year with actor Ryan Hurst in the role of Kratos. Unfortunately, Hurst got injured (after also putting in the work at the gym for the role ) and will be out of commission until next year. Amazon made the decision to recast the role and quickly hired Dave Bautista, who now has just a couple of months to get into Kratos-level shape. The show is expected to restart production in October, meaning Bautista won't have much time to rest.

The actor had recently lost a ton of weight and muscle after years of starring in action movies and being a professional wrestler. While Bautsita made sense as Kratos five years ago, some began to question if he was the right choice due to him being much slimmer. Bautista seems to be interested in proving the naysayers wrong and is hitting the weight room to get real beefy before stepping into the shoes of a gaming god.

Christopher Judge, the actor who plays Kratos in the current God of War games, revealed he auditioned to play the character in live-action . However, he ultimately took himself out of the running because he didn't want to work 12 - 18 hour days, have an intense diet, or work out constantly at 62 years old.
